description: Shared-DID human-agent identity model: human and agent share one DID with three verification methods (#0 identity key, #active human signing key, #agent agent signing key). stories.title: Create ADR-039: Shared-DID Human-Agent Identity Model
stories.description: Write ADR-039 in .docs/adrs/phase-1.md defining the shared-DID human-agent identity model. Decision: human and agent share one DID with #0 (identity key), #active (human signing key), #agent (agent signing key) verification methods. Rationale: mechanical enforcement of one-agent-per-context (verifiers reject DID documents with multiple #agent VMs), structural accountability (agent actions trace to human DID without UCAN chain resolution), protocol-native action provenance. Rejected alternative: separate DIDs linked by UCAN delegation — zero mechanical enforcement, agent identity structurally independent, human-agent unlinkability contradicts §9.1 invariant 1 and §4.5. Includes permission model (Categories A/B/C), enforcement stack (5 layers), and impacts on MLS, UCAN, inner envelope, key continuity, governance, and compromise recovery.

stories.title: Add UCAN kid header and key_scope to minting
stories.description: Add kid (Key ID) field to UCAN JWT header per RFC 7515 and add scp_key_scope to UCAN facts per ADR-039 acceptance criteria 6 and 8. The kid header identifies which verification method (#active or #agent) signed the UCAN token. The scp_key_scope fact field in the UCAN payload scopes the delegation: when present, the UCAN is only valid when presented by the specified key. Self-delegation (iss == aud, same DID) with key_scope is explicitly valid — this is how the human delegates specific permissions to the agent key. Update MintParams to include optional key_scope: Option<String>. Update token signing to include kid in JWT header.

stories.title: Add UCAN validation step 5b for key scope verification
stories.description: Add UCAN validation step 5b per ADR-039 acceptance criterion 7: after the existing audience check (step 5), if fct.scp_key_scope exists in the UCAN payload, verify that the presenting key matches the specified scope. The presenting key is identified by kid in the JWT header. If scp_key_scope is '#agent' but the presenter signed with #active (or vice versa), validation fails with UcanError::KeyScopeMismatch. If scp_key_scope is absent, skip this check (backward compatibility). This is a critical enforcement point: it ensures that UCANs scoped to the agent key cannot be exercised by the human key and vice versa.

stories.title: Implement ScpKeyCustodyAttestation type and DID document integration
stories.description: Implement ScpKeyCustodyAttestation per ADR-039 acceptance criterion 16 and Enforcement Stack layer 4. At identity creation, the DID document includes a service entry declaring key custody model. The attestation declares: custody_model (hardware-biometric, hardware-pin, software), platform (ios, android, desktop, browser), platform_attestation (optional platform-specific proof — Apple App Attest token or Android Key Attestation certificate chain). stories.title: Implement custody violation detection and permanent logging
stories.description: Implement ScpCustodyViolationAttestation per ADR-039 acceptance criteria 17-18 and Enforcement Stack layer 4. Unambiguous violations — Category A actions (DID document modifications) signed by #agent, or attestation mismatches with hardware proof — are permanently logged as ScpCustodyViolationAttestation records. These are append-only, never deleted. Create custody_violation.rs module in scp-core/src/trust/. Define violation types: CategoryAViolation (DID doc mod with #agent), AttestationMismatch (hardware proof contradicts behavior). DID owners can publish CounterAttestation records for reputation restoration. Violation records feed into trust evaluation (§7.1) as strong negative signals.

stories.title: Wire verifier-side Category A enforcement with violation logging
stories.description: Wire Enforcement Stack layer 3 (verifier validation) per ADR-039 acceptance criterion 15. All conformant verifiers must reject Category A actions (DID document modifications) signed by #agent. This is a network-level enforcement point: non-conformant SDKs can produce these signatures but they cannot propagate through the network. When a Category A action signed by #agent is detected, the verifier both rejects the action AND logs a ScpCustodyViolationAttestation (SCP-AB-019). Enforcement points: (1) UCAN validation — if the UCAN grants DID doc modification capability and kid is #agent, reject. (2) Inner envelope verification — if the action type is DID doc modification and signing_key_id is #agent, reject. Both rejection points call log_custody_violation() from SCP-AB-019.

details.note: Status corrected from a falsely-set 'done' (commit ac26cc5c, 2026-03-04, which bulk-flipped 22 stories to done in the implementation commit without independent verification). The persona dimension of the live message pipeline is now genuinely implemented and tested end-to-end through the public Supervisor::send_message (crates/scp-runtime/src/context/agent_binding_pipeline_tests.rs), replacing the prior component-only test that bypassed the Supervisor. Remaining before done: agent-key rotation propagation through the pipeline, Category-A rejection + custody-violation logging on the live receive path, three-VM key-continuity fingerprint, one-DID-one-vote; plus a production DID-document-backed KeyResolver. FFI/SDK per-message send-persona exposure (gate-ffi-bridges) is now advanced by the ADR-039 Enforcement-Stack Layer 2 persona-source seam: the native send bridges (PyO3, NAPI, UniFFI) no longer pin #active on the message-send path — each threads a pluggable per-send persona-source seam (a callable returning SigningKeyId, default #active, injected per bridge instance) feeding a persona-aware resolver so the #active/#agent stamp and the signing key are chosen atomically from one persona (fail-closed when #agent has no agent key); the scp-ffi WASM bridge has no send path (crates/scp-ffi/wasm does not exist), and the separate browser WASM client (scp-client / scp-client-wasm) provisions no agent key and does not route through scp-core's MessageSigner/CoreFields, so the persona seam is inapplicable there until scp-client gains agent-key custody (a real gap to revisit under RFC #2242 at that point), not an intrinsic absence. Category-A signing sites (root UCAN issuance, DID-document ops) remain hard-#active by design. This is plumbing only: the determiner (the policy that selects the persona non-forgeably) and Layer-1 custody-enforcement remain deferred to RFC #2242 (https://github.com/limn-works/scp/discussions/2242), so no accountability acceptance criterion (AC 4-5, 8-10) is satisfied by the seam alone.

stories.title: Update key continuity fingerprint and add negative tests
stories.description: Update key continuity fingerprint computation per ADR-039 acceptance criterion 12 and Key Continuity section. The fingerprint must include all three verification methods: identity_key, active_key, agent_key. Agent key absence uses domain-derived sentinel SHA-256("SCP-ABSENT-AGENT-KEY") to avoid Ed25519 identity point collision. Formula: fingerprint = SHA256("SCP-KEY-CONTINUITY-V1:" || len(did_a) || did_a || len(did_b) || did_b || a_identity || a_active || a_agent || b_identity || b_active || b_agent) with 4-byte big-endian length prefixes on DIDs. Add negative tests: (1) fingerprint changes when agent key is added, (2) fingerprint changes when agent key is rotated, (3) fingerprint changes when agent key is removed, (4) fingerprint with no agent key uses domain-derived sentinel, (5) DID document with multiple #agent VMs is rejected.

stories.title: Add the AgentPermissions fact type with parsing and validation
stories.description: Add the Rust type behind the UCAN fact fct.scp_agent_permissions per §4.9.2. The fact is a JSON object under the key scp_agent_permissions in a UCAN's fct map, with two required fields: v (integer format version, 1 today) and allow (array of {resource}:{action} strings carrying no scp:ctx:{context_id}/ prefix). This story creates the type, its serde representation, its parse-from-fct path, and its well-formedness validation. Chain resolution and enforcement are SCP-AB-024, not this story; minting is SCP-AB-026, not this story.
acceptanceCriteria: crates/scp-protocol/src/crypto/ucan/agent_permissions.rs declares a public struct AgentPermissions with fields v: u32 and allow: Vec<String>
AgentPermissions serializes to and deserializes from the JSON object {"v": 1, "allow": [...]} under the fct key scp_agent_permissions
A public fn parse_agent_permissions(fct: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<Option<AgentPermissions>, AgentPermissionsError> returns Ok(None) when the fct map has no scp_agent_permissions key
parse_agent_permissions returns Err when v is any value other than 1, and the error names the unsupported version
parse_agent_permissions returns Err when allow is absent, when allow is not an array, or when any entry is not a string
A well-formedness check rejects an allow entry that carries the scp:ctx: prefix, that contains more than one colon, or that has an empty resource or empty action segment
A well-formedness check accepts an asterisk only as the entire action segment (outlet_call:*) and rejects it in the resource position (*:read) and as a substring (outlet_ca*l:read, messages:wr*)
A public fn AgentPermissions::permits(&self, resource: &str, action: &str) -> bool returns true on an exact {resource}:{action} match and on a {resource}:* entry, and false otherwise
A public const fn default_agent_permissions() -> AgentPermissions returns v = 1 and allow = ["messages:read", "messages:write"]
Unit tests cover every accept and reject case named in the criteria above, including the three asterisk-placement rejections

stories.title: Enforce the agent permission set at UCAN validation step 6b
stories.description: Wire the permission set into the eleven-step UCAN chain validation at step 6b per §4.9.2 'How a validator reads it' and §7.2.1. When the presented token's kid is #agent, the verifier walks the prf chain from the leaf toward the root, takes the scp_agent_permissions of the first token whose kid is #active, falls back to the protocol default when no token on the chain carries the fact, and checks every capability in the presented token's att set against that permission set. A token whose kid is #active skips both steps. The fact type comes from SCP-AB-023.

stories.title: Reject a root UCAN signed by the agent key
stories.description: §4.9.1 reserves root UCAN issuance to #active: a root UCAN carries an empty prf, so its authority derives from the issuer's own key rather than from a parent token, and an agent that could issue one could grant itself every capability inside a context's ceiling. Sub-delegation stays Category B. Today enforce_ucan_category_a inspects only the capability resource type and never inspects prf, so an #agent-signed root token passes. Add the check at step 6b alongside the Category A resource check.

stories.title: Add agent-restricted roles to role assignment
stories.description: §4.9.3 lets a role assignment name a second role that applies when the signer is #agent. When the assignment names one, a capability check on an #agent-signed action reads that role's capability set; otherwise it reads the member's own role. The agent role's capability set MUST be a subset of the member's own role's set, so an agent never exceeds its human in the same context, and it MUST sit within the context's ceiling like any role definition (§5.5.1, §7.2.1).

stories.title: Add agent_rate_limit to ContextParams and count agent-signed actions against it
stories.description: §4.9.3 defines agent_rate_limit as an optional cap on how many actions signed by #agent a single member takes within a rolling window, on ContextParams, default absent. It bounds the agent persona only: an action signed by #active does not count against it. The cap denies an action once the window is full, which is what distinguishes it from the cost escalation of §19.7 — that mechanism reprices a high-velocity sender and never denies the send.

stories.title: Add agent_cosign_required to ContextParams and verify the human co-signature
stories.description: §4.9.3 defines agent_cosign_required as the list of capabilities that a member exercising them through #agent must additionally have signed with #active, on ContextParams, default empty. The list names capabilities rather than carrying a single boolean, because a context that required a human signature on every agent action would leave the agent nothing to do autonomously. When the invoked capability is on the list, the verifier requires a second signature over the same signed payload, produced by the #active verification method of the same DID.

stories.title: Publish the Category C parameters as structural metadata and change them through governance

stories.title: Intersect the Category B permission set with the Category C context restrictions
stories.description: §4.9.4 states that Category B and Category C answer different questions, so neither overrides the other: a verifier admits an #agent-signed action only when both answers permit it. The effective authority of an agent key in a context is the intersection of four bounds — Category B's permission set, the context's Category C parameters, the capabilities the token grants, and the context's capability ceiling — and no one of them widens another. This story adds the conformance tests that hold each direction, and fixes whichever check the tests find missing.
acceptanceCriteria: A test asserts an action Category B permits and the context's agent_keys_allowed forbids is rejected
A test asserts an action the context permits and the owner's Category B permission set omits is rejected
A test asserts an action both axes permit but the token's att set omits is rejected
A test asserts an action both axes permit and the token grants but the context's ceiling omits is rejected
A test asserts an action all four bounds permit is admitted
A test asserts no Category B permission set admits an #agent signature on a Category A capability
A test asserts no Category C parameter admits an #agent signature on a Category A capability
A test asserts no context parameter admits a UCAN over a capability reserved to #0
Every test above runs in crates/scp-testing/tests/integration/agent_binding.rs against the real validation pipeline, not against a helper called in isolation
